statement: The function returns a Bool r and r = true if and only if there exist integers i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(nums) and an integer n such that nums[i] + nums[i+1] + ... + nums[j] = n * k. If no such i, j, n exist, then r = false. This says exactly that nums has a contiguous subarray of length at least two whose sum is a multiple of k.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; sum_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[i] <= 2^31 - 1; and 1 <= k <= 2^31 - 1.

statement: The function returns a result on every input satisfying the preconditions: there exists a Bool b such that check_subarray_sum nums k = Result.ok b. It does not fail, panic, overflow, or access memory out of bounds.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; sum_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[i] <= 2^31 - 1; and 1 <= k <= 2^31 - 1.

statement: If there exist integers i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(nums) and an integer n such that sum_{t=i}^{j} nums[t] = n * k, then the function returns true.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; sum_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[i] <= 2^31 - 1; and 1 <= k <= 2^31 - 1.

statement: If the function returns true, then there exist integers i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(nums) and an integer n such that sum_{t=i}^{j} nums[t] = n * k.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; sum_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[i] <= 2^31 - 1; and 1 <= k <= 2^31 - 1.

statement: If len(nums) = 1, then the function returns false.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; sum_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[i] <= 2^31 - 1; and 1 <= k <= 2^31 - 1.

statement: If len(nums) >= 2, the function returns true; if len(nums) = 1, it returns false. Equivalently, for these inputs the result is true exactly when len(nums) >= 2.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; sum_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[i] <= 2^31 - 1; and k = 1.

statement: The function returns true if and only if there is an index i with 0 <= i < len(nums) - 1 such that nums[i] = 0 and nums[i+1] = 0.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; sum_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[i] <= 2^31 - 1; 1 <= k <= 2^31 - 1; and k > sum_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[i].

statement: If nums[i] ≡ nums'[i] (mod k) for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), meaning k divides nums[i] - nums'[i], then the Bool result returned for nums and k equals the Bool result returned for nums' and k.
preconditions: Both nums and nums' are slices with len(nums) >= 1, len(nums') = len(nums), len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000 and 0 <= nums'[i] <= 1000000000; sum_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[i] <= 2^31 - 1; sum_{i=0}^{len(nums')-1} nums'[i] <= 2^31 - 1; and 1 <= k <= 2^31 - 1.

statement: The Bool result returned for nums and k equals the Bool result returned for nums' and k, where nums' is the reversal of nums.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; sum_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[i] <= 2^31 - 1; 1 <= k <= 2^31 - 1; and nums' is a slice with len(nums') = len(nums) and nums'[i] = nums[len(nums)-1-i] for every 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: If check_subarray_sum nums k returns true, then check_subarray_sum nums' k returns true.
preconditions: Both nums and nums' are slices with len(nums) >= 1, len(nums') >= len(nums), len(nums') <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums'), 0 <= nums'[i] <= 1000000000; sum_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[i] <= 2^31 - 1; sum_{i=0}^{len(nums')-1} nums'[i] <= 2^31 - 1; 1 <= k <= 2^31 - 1; and there exists s with 0 <= s <= len(nums') - len(nums) such that nums'[s+i] = nums[i] for every 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Define pref(m) = sum_{t=0}^{m-1} nums[t] for 0 <= m <= len(nums), with pref(0) = 0. The function returns true if and only if there exist integers p and q with 0 <= p < q <= len(nums), q - p >= 2, and an integer n such that pref(q) - pref(p) = n * k.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; sum_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[i] <= 2^31 - 1; and 1 <= k <= 2^31 - 1.

statement: The function returns true if and only if nums[0] + nums[1] is a multiple of k, i.e. there exists an integer n such that nums[0] + nums[1] = n * k.
preconditions: len(nums) = 2; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; sum_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[i] <= 2^31 - 1; and 1 <= k <= 2^31 - 1.
